notes.note: All 1,287 actual source units inventoried before source review. Original flat-array refs, chapter values, anchors and wording are retained; Greek/Septuagint chapter divisions remain authoritative. No missing units are invented and inventory/import adds no completed review credit.

notes: Every one of the 139 source units has at least one retained supported pair; a target range counts as one pair.
Numbers 1:18 states first day of the month of the second year without the month number stated in 1:1; its source text remains unchanged.
The actual edition places the earlier 603,550 census figure at Exodus 39:3; the target key is not silently renumbered.

The edition gives Merari 6,050 at Numbers 3:34, Kohath 8,600 at 3:28, Gershon 7,500 at 3:22, and total Levi 22,000 at 3:39. The clan figures sum to 22,150; no reconciliation, emendation, or unsupported explanation is asserted. The excess-firstborn relation uses the explicitly stated 22,000 total, 22,273 firstborn, and 273 excess.

Numbers 4 service eligibility is twenty-five through fifty in these actual English records, distinguished from Numbers 3 population counts beginning at one month and Numbers 1 military counts beginning at twenty years.

Eliasaph son of Reuel (Gad) and Eliasaph son of Lael (Gershon) are not conflated; chief Elizaphan son of Uzziel is retained only with the explicit local Kohathite constituency, avoiding assumed identity across differing Elzaphan spellings.

Camp and departure parallels preserve the source orientation southwest, toward the sea, north, and east; the transport comparison preserves distinct Gershon/Merari and Kohath movements rather than harmonizing them into one asserted sequence.
All targets are confined to the authorized Saints canon; no Revelation text or excluded book is used.
Initial English-passage cross-reference pass; no claim of independent human specialist or Greek/Hebrew apparatus review.
Actual service age is twenty-five through fifty throughout Numbers 4; no familiar-edition thirty-year substitution.
Covering colours, items, carrying poles, shoulders, priestly supervision, non-touching and viewing precautions follow the actual English records, including the basin clause in Numbers 4:14.
Same-chapter entries deliberately identify command/fulfilment, specific introduction/content, summary/case, sequence, census population/count or component/total relations. They are labelled as such.

The jealousy law distinguishes concealed defilement, absent witnesses, jealous suspicion even where undefiled, conditional curses, and an unharmed clean outcome. No modern medical mechanism or current legal recommendation is inferred.
A subset of candidate passages was read for context but was not retained; reading and verification alone create no completion credit.
All 77 intrachapter relationship labels explicitly begin Same-chapter after peer audit. Final row counts remain 80 completed sources, 142 retained pairs and 175 distinct target units.
Preserved the actual chapter6 ending at verse26, with the divine-name statement within verse23; no customary verse27 was created.

Retained Numbers7 repetitions by linking each exact gift to its corresponding aggregate and later donors once to the first matching gift. Did not generate all pairwise combinations among twelve equivalent presentations.

The repeated donations preserve every donor, day, material, weight, animal category, sex, age and quantity. Aggregate links explain 2400 silver, 120 gold, twelve animals by category, twenty-four heifers and sixty of each deliverance group.
Preserved the actual twenty-five-year service threshold in Numbers4 and Numbers8, contrasting it with the twenty-year Chronicles arrangement.
Numbers8:26 is read according to its actual English subject, his brother, without importing a familiar alternative edition's wording.
Speech-introduction pairs identify the particular instruction and literary function of each speech, rather than merely comparing a generic revelation formula.

notes.note: Preserve the first-month anniversary and second-month exception, observed corpse impurity versus unexcused failure conditions, native/sojourner scope, meal and bone rules, and Moses' particular consultation. The later Chronicle postponement and impurity narrative retain their own circumstances and voices.

Cloud and fire, camping and departure, many days, a number of days, evening/morning/day/night and a month remain the source's stated cases. No new harmonized timetable or identical-date assumption is supplied.

Preserve two hammered silver trumpets, one-trumpet ruler summons, assembly versus departure signalling, all four actual directional signals, priestly association, war-in-the-land wording and calendar/offerings memorial. Later military and temple occasions are related examples, not silently identical legal settings.

Leader names/patronymics and the earlier camp formations are matched in their actual English. Gershon/Merari tent duties and Kohath holy-object carrying retain their distinct materials and conditions. The Tent-before-arrival pronoun wording is retained without independently assigning its unstated subject.

Preserve Hobab/Reuel, the refusal and renewed invitation, elder rather than an imported eyes wording, the ark's rest-search role, and actual34 prayer/35 rest/36 cloud order. Psalms67/80/131 keep Greek-edition references. The possible Hobab/Jobab identity in Judges4:11 is recorded pending and excluded from completed pairs.

notes: All84 source units have supported retained pairs, totaling113 pairs; each target range counts as one pair. No source is marked complete merely for import, inventory, pins, or technical validation.

Numbers11:25 explicitly says the elders prophesied and did not do so again; no alternative familiar rendering replaces it. Eldad and Medad remain enrolled men prophesying in camp without a new arithmetic reconciliation of the seventy.

Numbers11:32 preserves ten kors and cooled them in cooling places; no different unit, drying procedure, or supposed preservation method is supplied. Manna remains crystal in11:7 and oil-cake taste in11:8, distinct from Exodus16’s white and honey-cake description.
The broad Spirit/prophesy comparison with Acts2 does not identify Acts as quoting Moses, and the1Corinthians10 desire comparison does not select Numbers11 as its uniquely named example.

Numbers12 retains the Ethiopian wife and the reported family criticism, meekness, direct speech/glory, snow-like leprosy, confession, prayer, and seven-day exclusion. The12:3→12:13 relation is explicitly a character description read beside a particular narrative response, not an original-language or psychological proof. Exodus4 is not supplied a leprosy diagnosis absent from that actual text.

Scout names are preserved: Salamiel/Zaccur; Shaphat/Souri; Hoshea/Nun; Palti/Raphu; Gaddiel/Sodi for Zebulun; Gaddi/Susi for Manasseh; Ammiel/Gemalli; Sethur/Michael; Nahbi/Iabi; Gaddiel/Machi for Gad. Explicit13:16 renaming, rather than spelling conjecture, establishes Hoshea/Joshua.

Numbers13:20 remains days of spring, forerunners of grape harvest. Numbers13:21 remains Sin, Raab, Ephaath. Numbers13:22 retains Ahiman, Sheshai, Talmai and Hebron seven years before Tanis; no alternate sites or names replace them.

Graves of Craving/Graves of Desire and Ravine/Valley of the Cluster retain their actual differing English renderings. The former relation is labelled a particular verbal/narrative parallel without an independently asserted place-name equivalence. Numbers33’s Rithmah and12:16’s Paran are not silently harmonized.

Numbers13 and Deuteronomy1 retain their respective divine commissioning and the people’s request without reconstructing an unstated single sequence. The geographic inhabitants list in13:29 and Deuteronomy7’s seven nations are explicitly nonidentical.
Numbers 16 has 35 actual source units; bronze fire-pan memorials and subsequent congregation and staff material are actual Numbers 17, not silently imported into chapter16.
Preserved twenty-year registration threshold, Joshua/Caleb exceptions, children inheritance, forty exploration days and forty judgment years, and the actual herders and whoredom wording.
Number14:45 says Erman and names Amalek/Canaanites; Deuteronomy1:44 names Amorites and its own route ending Hormah. Parallel explanations preserve the distinct particulars.
Preserved each flour, oil and wine amount by lamb, ram and calf; Numbers28:7 says strong drink, whereas the Numbers15 lamb instruction says wine.

Unintentional communal and individual cases, prescribed animals, native/sojourner scope and presumptuous-hand destruction remain distinguished. Different Leviticus4 offerings are explicitly identified rather than harmonized.

The wood gatherer's observed act and custody awaiting determination are preserved; no claim that his act was merely suspected. All penalties are described as passage content, without current legal recommendations.
Numbers16:14 retains its actual Even if conditional and eye-gouging accusation, rather than a familiar-edition negative statement. Numbers16:15 says desirable possession, not a substituted donkey.

Numbers26:11 expressly says Korah's sons did not die; no claim of universal descendant destruction is made. The possible source of 2Timothy2:19 wording is expressed as a particular parallel without exclusive quotation-source identification.
All retained relationships are initial English-passage curation. No independent human specialist, Greek, Hebrew or apparatus approval is claimed.

Preserved every actual chapter17 unit in its 28-unit order: bronze fire-pan memorial, renewed grumbling and outbreak, then the named-staff test and Israel's fear. No familiar-edition chapter17 numbering was substituted.

Chapter17 staff results say nuts; no unprovided species or flowering detail was added. The text specifies preservation before the testimonies, while Hebrews9:4 is described according to its own wording without harmonizing the placement formulations.
Distinguished Eleazar taking the fire pans from the plural application to the altar; in chapter19 the animal is slaughtered before Eleazar and other handlers have distinct tasks.
Maintained touch versus approach restrictions and their actual actors; Israel's fearful statement is distinguished from the specific outsider and Levitical/priestly access rules.

Priestly male-only most-holy portions, clean-household portions including daughters, and Levitical wages eaten anywhere are distinguished. Numbers18:10 location wording is not silently replaced by the court wording of Leviticus.
Firstborn human and unclean-livestock redemption, nonredeemable firstborn cattle/flock, five-shekel valuation, twenty-obol standard, and one-month age are preserved.
Tithe receipts, tithe of the tithe, priestly recipient, agricultural reckoning, and household wage remain distinct; no later administrative detail is imported into the earlier instruction.

Corpse contact causes seven-day uncleanness; continued failure to receive purification is the specified condition of the sanctuary-defilement sanction. Contact alone is not described as automatically incurring that sanction.
Preserved third/seventh-day sprinkling, seventh-day washing/bathing, remaining evening uncleanness, and different requirements for priest, burner, ash collector, sprinkler and water toucher.
No modern medical mechanism, independent historical proof, or present-day legal prescription is inferred.

After peer precision review, the reciprocal Numbers18:27 and18:30 links preserve the agricultural reckoning language and the after-firstfruits condition without resolving the pronoun beyond the supplied text.

notes.note: Preserve Zin/Kadesh, Miriam’s death, the command to speak versus two narrated strokes, the stated unbelief/sanctification judgment and actual water names. Psalms105:33 says issued a command with his lips, not an imported rashly phrase; the staff’s individual ownership and angel identity are not newly resolved.

Preserve diplomatic terms, the offered water payment, Edom’s refusal and detour, Hor and Eleazar’s garment succession, and thirty-day mourning. Deuteronomy10:6 names Misadai; the cross-reference compares Aaron’s death/succession without identifying that place with Hor. The fortieth-year date is explicitly supplied by Numbers33, not invented in20:1.

Preserve Atharim, the devotion place-name, deadly serpents and bronze standard, the stated source’s Achel-gai/Gai forms, Zered and Arnon, Zoob and Er in the book citation, and the rulers/kings digging the well. Do not import a formal book title, place-name equivalence or familiar nobles-with-staves wording.

Preserve distinct Edom/Sihon embassies, water terms, Jahaz, Arnon/Jabbok/Ammon limits, Heshbon’s prior Moabite war, the poem’s women-and-fire wording, Jazer and Og at Edrei. Greek-numbered Psalms134/135 and explicit later New Testament interpretations keep their actual source references.
